There are many ways to cook a steak, but to get it right every time try the reverse sear method.
1) Season steak with sea salt, black pepper and/or seasoning of choice. Make sure the seasoning has a healthy amount of salt in it.
2) Let rest at room temperature for one hour per inch of thickness on a cooling rack. This prevents excess moisture from collecting on the bottom of the steak. This was a 2" thick boneless ribeye which rested at room temperature for about two hours.
3) Insert meat thermometer into steak, place into a cold oven, and turn oven to 170 - 200 degrees.
4) Cooking steak in oven until it is 5 to 10 degrees below your target temperature. I like my steaks about 125-130 so this was pulled at 155 degrees.
5) Use a papertowel to soak up any exterior moisture on the steak. We want the surface of the steak to be as dry as possible. Then re-season with salt and pepper.
6) To finish your steak you can either use a very hot preheated grill, charcoal is best, or a very hot cast iron or other heavy pan. I, however, prefer the "afterburner method" which gives you heat in excess of 1,000 degrees.
7) To use the afterburner method:
a) Place a charcoal chimney over a grill or heat resistant surface.
b) Fill the chimney halfway with natural lump charcoal.
c) Wet a paper towel with vegetable oil and place on grill grate or heat resistant surface.
d) Ignite the paper towel placing the chimney over it.
e) Place grate over top of chimney and allow to preheat until all charcoal is ignited and glowing red.
8) Place steak on grate searing for 1 minute per side rotating 45 degrees at the 30 second mark.
9) After searing the steak for one minute on both sides, remove steak to cutting board.
10) Top steak with butter, tent loosely with foil, and let rest for 10-15 minutes depending on thickness.
11) Slice steak across the grain and serve.

Enjoy!
